acceptance: A deliberately failing slow test on a branch (dispatch nightly-v2 on that branch, or the workflow's existing dry path) produces a failed slow domain/status; reverting it produces success. Run ids recorded in context.
The duration refresh still runs and uploads its artifact when slow tests fail.
`docs/internal/nightly-t3.md` lists the slow domain and what fails it; `tests/unit/workflows/test_nightly_t3_workflow.py` asserts that exit code 1 from the slow tier fails the domain.
No slow test is skipped, deselected or marked to make the domain green.
context: Filed 2026-11-19 from the remediation of 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-19.
description:
Problem. The only CI job that runs `slow` tests is nightly-v2.yml `t3:durations` ("Measure slow tier durations"). It exits non-zero only when pytest's code is greater than 1, so ordinary test failures (code 1) pass. Evidence: nightly 44386073922 on b5b584ef77 (2026-11-18), job 135090909465 `t3:durations | duration refresh` concluded success while its log reads "3 failed, 700 passed": the three TPC-H maintenance tests that #4337 broke (fixed later by #4372). Nobody saw the breakage until a local full-suite run.
Expected outcome. A slow-test failure on develop is reported as a failed nightly domain the morning after, without losing the duration refresh.

## Decision gate
(agent, record in context before coding): choose between (a) a separate `t3:slow` domain that runs the slow tier and fails on any test failure, with `t3:durations` reading its junit for timings, or (b) keeping one job but publishing a failed `t3:slow` status when the slow exit code is 1 while still uploading durations. Pick the one that adds no second full slow run (about 55 min) unless the owner approves the runner cost. Record why.

## Guardrails
- Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`, `make agent-write-preflight`); never edit the primary clone.
- No skip, xfail, rerun marker, raised timeout or weakened assertion to turn a check green.
- Heavy work only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point; no admission or watchdog override.
- No live vendor cloud without owner approval in the task.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (`make comment-policy-check`); user-facing changes add a `changelog.d/` fragment.
- Anchors (file:line, run ids) are orientation from 2026-11-19; re-read before editing and stop to update the item on a mismatch.
- Do not change the fast or medium tier selection.
- Do not remove `--timeout=1200` or `-n 0` from the slow run.
